text:
mira: Quick follow-up from the RFC review — we touched on exposing abuse signals into the fairness scheduler but didn't land an interface. Brainstorming here: how do we provide useful signals without creating an attack surface (clients learning the exact heuristics)?

danielle: we should avoid a raw score endpoint. instead surface a monotonic bucket + decay window. e.g. 'score_bucket: high/med/low', 'decay_seconds: 3600' — opaque enough and actionable by scheduler.

sam: agree on buckets, + I'd add a signed freshness token so downstream can't game by replaying old good states. HMAC with short TTL.

lee: another thought — split signals into two channels: synchronous admission hints (buckets) and asynchronous forensic vectors (detailed features) for SRE/security. scheduler only gets the buckets.

mira: +1 to separation. also want to make sure the scheduler can still do proportional fairness within 'high' bucket. need numeric subscore but derived server-side, not client-visible.

danielle: propose API surface: 
```
GET /v1/sidecar/heuristic?client_id=XXX
Response: {"bucket":"high","ttl":30,"nonce":"abc123.hmac"}
```
we document TTL meaning: recompute on every admission. keep response tiny to limit fingerprinting.

sam: on the HMAC nonce, we should include route/model context and a salt per-region to prevent cross-probing. also rate-limit this endpoint heavily and sample responses for low-risk clients.

lee: operationally we need telemetry hooks: how often bucket flips, %requests scored, and false-positive rate tied to billing alerts. suggest small rollout: 1% traffic -> 10% -> 100% with canary for critical tenants.

mira: tradeoffs: more opaque = harder to tune fairness parameters. ops wants explainability when tenants complain. maybe keep an internal debug mode that logs vector -> bucket mapping but gated to a security role and sampling.

danielle: agreed. add an 'explain' flag on internal sidecar only, never on public API. audit log every explain.

security-bot: Reminder: run penetration test on any public scoring endpoint. See checklist: https://redwood.internal/sec/checklists/heuristic-api

sam: flags for RFC: 1) API proto (bucket + ttl + nonce), 2) HMAC scheme + salt rotation plan, 3) telemetry + explain-mode gating, 4) rollout plan + sampling, 5) failure modes (always-backoff, fallback to cost-first). I'll draft an RFC PR with examples.

lee: one more: scheduler contract needs an erasure-tolerant admission call. if scoring endpoint times out, scheduler should fall back to default fair-share computed from token quotas. document SLOs for scoring endpoint: p99 < 5ms.

mira: good list. action items: @sam make RFC draft, @danielle sketch sidecar proto, @lee ops rollout playbook, I'll coordinate security pen-test. aim for RFC week after next. :+1:

sam: sounds good, will start draft today and tag folks.

mira: thanks all. keeping this tight will avoid leaking heuristics while giving scheduler enough signal for graceful degradation.
